findings.reason: event_service.ts:5 declares isRegistered as async, and the controller tests `!this.eventService.isRegistered(user!, event)` without await. A Promise is always truthy, so the rejection branch never runs and checkin attaches any scanned participant who is not already checked in.
findings.claim: Unregistered participants can be checked in because the isRegistered check is not awaited.
findings.evidence: EventService.isRegistered is async, so `!this.eventService.isRegistered(user!, event)` tests a truthy Promise and always skips rejection. For a valid participant who is neither registered nor checked in, execution reaches checkin at line 116; the service attaches the user without another registration check. Executing the handler with isRegistered resolving false confirmed this path.

findings.reason: page.tsx:290 wraps the only QrCode trigger (line 313-315) inside `{!isRegistered && ...}`, and the controller computes isRegistered for the logged-in user. A registered staff member therefore has no way to set scannerModalOpen. Lowered to medium because it only affects staff who registered themselves.
findings.claim: Staff who are registered for an event cannot open its check-in scanner.
findings.evidence: The only control that sets scannerModalOpen to true is nested inside `!isRegistered` at line 290. EventsController.show calculates registration for the current user, so a registered staff member loses that control while the dialog remains closed.

findings.reason: The controller awaits isCheckedIn and then checkin attaches without handling the error, while the migration adds UNIQUE(event_id,user_id). scanner.tsx sets allowMultiple={true} and scanDelay={0}, so one QR can send duplicate posts close together, and the losing insert returns a 500 instead of 'already checked in'.
findings.claim: Concurrent check-ins of the same participant raise an unhandled unique-constraint error.
findings.evidence: EventsController.checkin separately awaits isCheckedIn and then calls checkin. Two requests can both observe no check-in before this unconditional attach. The migration enforces UNIQUE(event_id,user_id), but neither the service nor controller handles the losing insert as an already-checked-in result.

members.claim: Concurrent check-ins for the same participant can produce an unhandled database error.

findings.reason: The result of User.findBy at line 104 is used with `user!` without a null check, and isCheckedIn dereferences user.id. The schema link is user→profile (users.participantProfileId is nullable), so an orphan profile is possible but the code doesn't show how one would arise. Lowered to low.
findings.claim: A participant profile with no linked user causes an exception instead of a not-found message.
findings.evidence: The controller checks whether the profile exists but never checks the result of User.findBy. A null user is passed to isRegistered and isCheckedIn, both of which dereference user.id. The profile-to-user association is not guaranteed by the schema; ProfilesController.index explicitly handles this same missing-user state.
